items.title: St. Louis Fed's Musalem says four more rate hikes may be needed in coming months
items.summary: The forecast represents one of the most hawkish views among policymakers.
items.body: St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem indicated Tuesday that the central bank may need as many as four rate hikes in coming months, offering one of the most hawkish views yet by a Fed policymaker about the steps needed to quell inflation. During a speech delivered in Argentina, Musalem made the case that current policy is not significantly restricting economic activity. "The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve 2% inflation in a timely manner," he said. Musalem said the real policy rate, which subtracts the inflation rate from the Fed's target rate, needs to be between 2%-2.5% by next spring, and estimated that the current rate is about a full point below that range. That position suggests the Fed may need to hike at each of the upcoming Fed meetings in December, January, March and April.

items.title: Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings
items.summary: Nvidia options are pricing in a bigger move than usual.
items.body: Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting big moves. With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters. Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25.

items.title: Nvidia reports bumper results as firm says it not reinstating Huang
items.summary: Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang earlier on Tuesday offered to return, despite the board's disinterest.
items.body: Nvidia's quarterly sales doubled to top $100bn for the first time as the company insisted it is not reinstating ousted founder Jensen Huang. In the company's first results since Huang's dramatic exit, interim chief executive Collette Kress said Nvidia's "roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater". The company's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier, reaching $115.8bn (£86.9bn), with shares in the company recovering some recent losses in after-hours trading. Earlier on Tuesday Huang, said he would be "honoured" to return and lead Nvidia, having quit following two alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a possible spy for China. "The board does not intend to reinstate him," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones told investors on Tuesday. The company's profits also doubled from a year ago. For the quarter, which covered the three months to October 25, profit hit $65bn.

items.title: Milburn calls for tax cuts for businesses hiring young people despite union concerns
items.summary: Youth unemployment review risks clash with unions and Labour left over workers’ rights and minimum wage Neet ideas: what’s in Alan Milburn’s youth unemployment report? Who are the Neets? UK youth job crisis in five charts Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on young people…
items.body: Alan Milburn has called on ministers to cut business taxes and ease regulations to encourage employers to hire more young people, setting up a potential clash with trade unions and the Labour left over employment rights. The former health secretary published the results of his year-long review into youth unemployment on Wednesday, in what the prime minister, Andy Burnham , called a “watershed moment” for young people. But while ministers embraced his central recommendation of cutting benefit and sickness payments to pay for more concerted employment support, his recommendations on workers’ rights, national insurance and the minimum wage pose potentially awkward dilemmas for the government.

items.title: Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair
items.summary: Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.
items.body: Nvidia on Tuesday said it had created a board-level national security and export-control committee. This follows the scandal surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang , who resigned last week over extramarital affairs , including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and working to help ensure higher quality chips crucial to AI development made it to the Chinese market. The events have heightened oversight of the US tech giant and its importance to national security, as well as wiping several hundred billion dollars off the stock market valuation of what investors treat as the world's most valuable company in the space of a month. Since Huang's resignation, some investors — including Elon Musk and Donald Trump — have voiced concern that his departure could leave Nvidia and America's AI sector in peril and are now calling for his return.

items.summary: Major outages showcase the risks of interconnected tech in the age of AI.
items.body: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton dismissed suspicions that malicious activity led to a series of outages at major tech firms and government agencies over the past week. "This is not cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state," he told CNBC's "Closing Bell" on Tuesday. "We've looked very closely." It's been a tough few days for the technology world after a series of widespread disruptions brought different parts of life to a halt. On Tuesday, an outage halted internal communications at the National Security Agency, and iPhone maker Apple confirmed that different products were either down or having issues . The NSA pointed to "scheduled routine maintenance," while Apple cited "an internal update" as the reason behind its issues.

items.title: Analysis: The Fed's chairman sees an AI revolution coming. Now he has to figure out what it means
items.summary: Kevin Warsh sees AI at a turning point. He faces tough questions on jobs and interest rates.
items.body: Artificial intelligence is about to sweep through the economy. The Federal Reserve is bracing for impact. "We are at a hinge point in the U.S. economy," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said at a conference he convened in San Francisco on Monday. But exactly when and how the economy could turn, and what that means for interest rates and inflation, isn't yet clear. The meeting of Warsh's AI task force saw the new Fed chairman publicly asking the questions Americans will ultimately expect him to answer. He hinted at a few of his private views on whether white-collar workers could soon face massive job losses , but he largely left the speculation to an array of experts he has assembled to advise the Fed. With the technology racing ahead, Warsh won't be able to put off giving his own answers much longer.

items.title: Jensen Huang says he would be 'honoured' to return as Nvidia CEO if board asked him
items.summary: Huang says he has had an "outpouring" of calls from investors and others calling for him to return.
items.body: Jensen Huang said he would be "honoured" to return as the boss of tech giant Nvidia if the board asked him to, in his first public comments since his shock resignation. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely," Huang said on X, days after reports he had extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy. He said he had an "outpouring" of calls from company employees, investors and others calling for him to return as CEO of Nvidia. But, as the BBC reported on Monday, Nvidia's board is not considering bringing him back to lead the company. The company's board is investigating his conduct , which includes an alleged affair with an Nvidia executive. The AI chip giant is set to report its financial results later on Tuesday, during which the company's interim chief executive, Collette Kress, may address the situation with Huang.

items.title: Some EU countries ‘could accept unlimited young Britons’ under youth mobility scheme
items.summary: Scheme expected to be sealed in principle at EU-UK summit in Brussels on Friday but trickier elements could be postponed for six months EU countries including Germany could accept an unlimited number of young Britons under a youth mobility scheme, according to sources. Fresh…
items.body: EU countries including Germany could accept an unlimited number of young Britons under a youth mobility scheme, according to sources. Fresh details on how a scheme might work have emerged with EU leaders and the UK expected to settle on a quota of about 100,000 a year being allowed to work, travel or study in each others territories from 2028. The UK has insisted on a quota of EU citizens entering the UK under the scheme to guard against mass migration, but some countries have said they will not follow suit on the other side of the Channel and would be open to taking unlimited numbers. The quota is expected to be worked out on a country-by-country basis with smaller countries such as Malta and Luxembourg seeking a system that will not be based on a per-capita quota per EU member state.

items.summary: Congress members are pushing for a series of chip-related export control bills to be included in the annual National Defense Authorization Act.
items.body: Revelations about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy have reinvigorated a congressional push to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence technology. Federal lawmakers are pushing to include several measures to tighten export controls on advanced chips and related technologies in the final version of the National Defense Authorization Act. Congress is expected to consider the must-pass package that authorizes defense funding in December. Those proposals were included as amendments to an earlier version of the NDAA, which Senate Democrats blocked in July and have not been adopted by either congressional chamber in the interim.

items.title: We can't afford to hire under-25s, say firms. Will Milburn plans help?
items.summary: The proposal to cut employers' National Insurance costs is "essential" to tackling the Neet problem, one business group says.
items.body: Lowering employers' National Insurance (NI) payments for those between 21 and 24, and cash incentives to take on some workers are among proposals put forward in Alan Milburn's report to get more 18-24 year-olds working. Many companies have complained that recent increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage have made it more expensive to take on staff. We talked to firms and business groups about the issues they face when hiring younger works and what they make of the proposals. Cutting NI costs is "right in the sweet spot of what firms need to hit the hire button", said the Recruitment and Employment Confederation (REC). The Milburn report proposes NI thresholds could be raised over the next five years, from £5,000 to £10,000 for those aged 21 to 24, and suggests prioritising the retail and hospitality sectors.

items.title: Where are the most jobs for 18-24 year-olds?
items.summary: How many jobs are there where you live and in which sectors are you most likely to find an opening?
items.body: If you're one of the nearly one million people aged 16-24 not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet" - then you might be wondering where to start. Under-25s should be guaranteed job placements or training to help them find permanent work, a major review aimed at cutting the number of Neets will say. The Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) think tank used online job adverts to help identify the number of vacancies suitable for young people in the area they live, relative to the size of the local population. It used AI to help identify the jobs, which were broadly defined as roles requiring relatively low experience or education. According to its analysis, South Oxfordshire had 387 suitable vacancies per 1,000 18 to 24-year-olds in the area - the most of any local authority. Rotherham had the least, at 53 per 1,000.

items.title: Deutsche Bank dismissed warnings about dealings with risky clients, reports claim
items.summary: International investigation using trove of leaked internal data allegedly shows German bank overlooked compliance concerns to safeguard profits Deutsche Bank reportedly dismissed warnings about its dealings with risky clients, including high-profile Russian oligarchs, to protect…
items.body: Deutsche Bank reportedly dismissed warnings about its dealings with risky clients, including high-profile Russian oligarchs, to protect profits, the findings of an investigation into a trove of leaked bank documents indicate. A leak of 15m internal files is reported to show that the troubled German bank repeatedly ignored concerns by its compliance officers about its risk-taking, despite having already been caught being used to launder billions of dollars for Russian criminals, spies and oligarchs between 2010 and 2015. The investigations, which were published by media outlets including Der Spiegel, the Financial Times, the New York Times and Le Monde, will represent a fresh blow for Deutsche Bank, which has struggled to repair its reputation after a number of scandals and dealings with controversial clients including the US president, Donald Trump, and the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

items.body: The UK unemployment rate has unexpectedly fallen as the government released an important report on the youth jobs crisis . The unemployment rate was 4.6% in September, dipping from 4.7% in August and down from 5% earlier in the year, according to the Office for National Statistics . However, the number of vacancies fell as employers delayed hiring in response to global economic uncertainty and the use of artificial intelligence, which many analysts expect will lead to widespread job losses. Business groups said the slump in vacancies posed a problem for the government as responded to Alan Milburn’s report on young people not in employment, education or training (Neets) .

items.title: We couldn't afford a house alone, so we bought one with strangers
items.summary: People who can't afford to get on the housing ladder are buying homes with someone they don't know.
items.body: When Elizabeth and Tom Wilcox realised they could never afford to buy the home they wanted for themselves and their two children, they decided to take a leap of faith. They'd find another couple with young kids, complete strangers to them, and propose that they go halves on a property and all move in together. Based in Vancouver, which has long had some of the highest house prices in Canada, the Wilcoxes were desperate to buy a home that had a back garden for their children to play in. "We wanted a house with a yard that could fit a trampoline, in a walkable neighbourhood, but we couldn't afford it," says Elizabeth, a project manager in the healthcare sector. With a budget of C$1m ($700,000; £500,000) all they could hope for was a small apartment with a balcony at best.

items.title: Former WH Smith chain TG Jones put up for sale after closing 130 stores
items.summary: Modella Capital plans auction of high street retailer, which employs about 3,500 people, next year The owner of TG Jones is exploring a potential sale less than 18 months after completing a deal to buy the high street chain formerly known as WH Smith. Modella Capital, which also…
items.body: The owner of TG Jones is exploring a potential sale less than 18 months after completing a deal to buy the high street chain formerly known as WH Smith. Modella Capital, which also owns businesses including Hobbycraft, completed a deal to buy the 233-year-old business for £42m in June last year. The company, which pushed through a swingeing restructure to close more than 100 stores after receiving high court approval in July, has moved to appoint advisers after receiving unsolicited expressions of interest for the business. Modella, which has closed about 150 of the 480 WH Smith stores since taking control, has appointed the corporate finance arm of Teneo, according to Sky News which first reported the news. “High-street retailer TG Jones has received unsolicited offers for the business,” said Modella and TG Jones in a joint statement.

items.title: Nvidia warns chip buyers of legal risks tied to China AI access, sources tell CNBC
items.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department is making moves to tighten export controls.
items.body: Nvidia warned its customers that new legislation on Chinese companies remotely accessing its artificial-intelligence chips could expose it and them to U.S. "legal action," sources told CNBC. The chip giant is facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips, which U.S. export controls restrict from going to China. Nvidia messaged chip buyers in recent months to caution that the proposed Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services in the same way as physical hardware, potentially exposing both parties to legal risk, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The people asked not to be named while discussing private communications.

items.title: How new US chip restrictions on South East Asia will hit China
items.summary: The new rules restrict chip exports and also access to their computing power, which China relies on heavily.
items.body: As US President Donald Trump heads to China, his administration has renewed efforts to curb Beijing's access to advanced semiconductors. On Monday, Washington announced new interim rules that will increase scrutiny of data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. The move not only restricts the export of advanced chips, but also access to their computing power, which Chinese firms currently rent abroad to train artificial intelligence (AI) models. South East Asian countries in particular have invested heavily in data centres to power their AI ambitions - and Chinese firms seeking computing power overseas have been a key market. But now these firms will need a US government licence to buy advanced chips from Nvidia or other American chipmakers.

items.title: Santander allows staff to count holidays and sick leave as days worked in office
items.summary: News of Spanish-owned lender’s policy emerges as other banks are toughening their stance on working from home Staff at the high street bank Santander have been permitted to log holiday and sick leave as days worked in the office, helping them to meet workplace attendance…
items.body: Staff at the high street bank Santander have been permitted to log holiday and sick leave as days worked in the office, helping them to meet workplace attendance requirements. Back-office staff at the Spanish-owned lender have been expected to spend at least 12 working days each month in what the company calls a “head office location”, although this does not apply to staff working in bank branches. However, at the same time as other banks are toughening their stance on the rights of employees to work from home , it has emerged that a peculiarity in the lender’s system means that workers are marked as being at their desk even when they are on annual leave or off work because of illness. The company has its UK headquarters in Milton Keynes, England, and has offices in Glasgow and central London.

items.title: Demis Hassabis’ AI company raises $5 billion, months after he left as Google DeepMind CEO
items.summary: Isomorphic Labs is looking to develop new medicines using AI.
items.body: Isomorphic Labs, an artificial intelligence drug discovery startup founded by former Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis, has raised a $5 billion Series C, the company said on Tuesday. Isomorphic's round comes three-and-a-half months after Hassabis stepped back as CEO of DeepMind, Google's AI lab, which he co-founded before the Big Tech giant acquired it in 2014. The round was co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, alongside Andreessen Horowitz, with investment from Alphabet , Google's parent. The fresh funds will help fund the design and development of new medicines using AI. Drug discovery startups have seen record funding poured into them by investors in 2026 as companies look to capitalize on advances in AI. OpenAI and Anthropic have also been investing in tools to develop new medicines using the technology.

items.summary: The Singapore-based company is suspected of helping to ship high-end AI chips from tech giant Nvidia to China, violating US export rules.
items.body: The United States has confirmed it is investigating computing company Megaspeed, suspecting it of violating US export controls by helping to ship tech giant Nvidia's chips to China. In a joint statement, the US Department of Justice and Department of Commerce said they had been investigating Singapore-based firm Megaspeed since 2024. It comes after questions were raised about the possibility high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions. Concerns emerged in recent weeks after Nvidia founder Jensen Huang revealed he had an extramarital affair , allegedly with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. US authorities suspect her of spying for Beijing, which China denies. Jensen Huang resigned from his role as chief executive last week following revelations he had two affairs.

items.body: Ikea has ditched some planned store openings in the UK blaming the cost of business taxes , which it said were the highest in Europe. As its annual UK sales little more than flatlined at the Swedish flatpack furniture retailer, its UK boss, David McCabe, said: “There are locations where we were planning to open a new unit, and those plans have been abandoned due to the cost that we experience and the complexity within the market. “I would hope that we’re able to bring those projects back to life,” he added. “But it’s a very real impact here in the UK, when those investments will go to other countries in Europe.” The planned investments were smaller UK stores, but the retailer declined to comment on exact locations. Ikea has been pushing further into smaller high street shops , rather than its traditional out-of-town outlets.

items.summary: Data center policy has become a key election issue in Spain, creating an obstacle to existing deals and potentially costing billions of dollars in investment.
items.body: Spain's government is seeking to tighten restrictions on one of Europe's fastest-growing data center booms, as the country's Socialist prime minister prepares to fight an election. Investors like Amazon, Microsoft and Blackstone-backed QTS are on tenterhooks. The measure, which doesn't need parliamentary approval, could be approved by Pedro Sánchez's cabinet by next week, and is widely expected to pass ahead of the Nov. 29 elections. It could potentially cost one of Europe's fastest-growing tech regions billions of dollars in investment. The government first introduced the decree in August, partly in response to concerns over energy demand and prices. After fierce opposition, it put forward a revised version on Oct. 26, but the proposal still includes strict renewable-energy requirements.

items.title: Government must act now or lose Royal Mail, former minister warns
items.summary: The former business secretary says "undercutting" by rivals will make Royal Mail "unviable".
items.body: Former Business Secretary Peter Kyle has said the government must act urgently to "level the playing field" for Royal Mail or risk the business becoming unviable. He said he was concerned that the firm was being "undercut" by rival parcel delivery firms who did not employ staff under the same conditions. Royal Mail, which is owned by International Distribution Services, has struggled in recent years with increased competition, fewer letters being sent and fines from the regulator for missing delivery targets. A government spokesperson said it would consider whether further reforms are required to the parcel market after the watchdog, Ofcom, publishes its annual monitoring report in December.

items.title: Hoping for Britain to rejoin the EU with Andy Burnham? You may be waiting a long time | Timothy Garton Ash
items.summary: The PM’s first big speech on the UK and Europe was cautious and disappointing. Don’t expect any great leaps towards a new deal Ever since Andy Burnham became the British prime minister this summer, people all over Europe have been asking me one question: “Will the UK rejoin the…
items.body: E ver since Andy Burnham became the British prime minister this summer, people all over Europe have been asking me one question: “Will the UK rejoin the EU?” Sometimes they add: “And if so, when?” None of the intermediate options between the current hard Brexit and Brejoin are of any interest at all to most other Europeans. Measured against these great expectations, Burnham’s first big speech on Britain and Europe, delivered on Monday evening amid all the pomp and circumstance the City of London could furnish, must be considered a disappointment. It was both a cautious and a curiously old-fashioned speech. Cautious in diagnosis: his bold statement that “we have lost more than we have gained in the last 10 years” was immediately followed by “the hard Brexit we were given is not good enough for Britain”.

items.title: South Korea will suspend all aircraft operation for 35 minutes and markets will open late. Here’s why
items.summary: South Korea will suspend aircraft takeoffs and landings nationwide for 35 minutes on Thursday to minimize noise during a college entrance exam.
items.body: South Korea will suspend all aircraft takeoffs and landings nationwide for 35 minutes on Thursday to minimize noise during the English listening portion of the country's highly competitive college entrance exam, the government said Tuesday. The restrictions will be in place from 1:05 p.m. to 1:40 p.m. local time, affecting 130 flights, including 81 international and 49 domestic services, according to the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport. Planes already in the air will be required to remain at least 3 kilometers above the ground during the exam, while emergency flights will be exempt from the restrictions. The measures will also apply to helicopters, light aircraft and drones, with all drone flights prohibited nationwide during the 35 minutes. Violators could face criminal penalties, the ministry said.

items.title: OpenAI sued by California over Hugging Face attack
items.summary: Attorney General Rob Bonta alleges that the artificial intelligence misled and endangered the public.
items.body: California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI on Monday, alleging the ChatGPT-maker misled and endangered the public by developing artificial intelligence (AI) models without proper safeguards. In the lawsuit, Bonta cited the July 2026 attack on the AI platform Hugging Face by experimental OpenAI agents which accessed the internet to breach that company's internal systems. Bonta claimed OpenAI created a public nuisance and violated the state's unfair competition laws. OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri told the BBC in a statement that Bonta's lawsuit "appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab". Other major AI developers including Anthropic, Meta, and Google have also said their models have staged similar attacks.

items.title: The Guardian view on the Milburn report: a manifesto for youth participation | Editorial
items.summary: This is not a rerun of failed welfare cuts, but young people who rely on benefits cannot be expected to take promised opportunities on trust The gap between the state’s investment in young people compared with older generations has more than doubled in two decades. At the same…
items.body: T he gap between the state’s investment in young people compared with older generations has more than doubled in two decades. At the same time, the number of 16- to 24-year-olds who are neither in education, employment or training (Neet) has climbed to 1 million. In Europe, only Romania has a higher Neet rate. Alan Milburn’s message is that this amounts to a “moral crisis” which the British state must urgently address. Asked to write a review about young people and work , he has produced a “manifesto” for placing the broken social contract between generations at the heart of government. On Tuesday, his proposals for far-reaching changes to welfare, health, education and employment were on their way to becoming government policy as he was chosen to lead a new Youth Opportunities Unit.

items.title: Nvidia closes lower ahead of earnings as company reels from Huang resignation
items.summary: Investors have been weighing the fallout from former CEO Jensen Huang's resignation.
items.body: Nvidia shares closed marginally lower Tuesday as former CEO Jensen Huang released his first public statement since his resignation and the company prepares to report earnings after the bell. In the statement, Huang said he is open to returning as Nvidia's CEO and that he is committed to cooperating with the board's investigation into his behavior. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang said in a statement obtained by CNBC's David Faber . "I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation." "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang continued.

items.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex boss
items.summary: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
items.body: Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for the company's co-founder Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, supported the effort. Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, joining a list of supporters including SpaceX's Elon Musk who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign. But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in reinstating him after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs , including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy. The same day, the White House also said it will further restrict China's access to AI chips from firms like Nvidia. The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance.

items.title: Will the Milburn review come good or go south? Either way, we’ll always have Eurovision
items.summary: The announcement of state plans to engage with young people told us nothing we hadn’t already heard, but it still felt momentous It’s one of the country’s worst kept secrets. There can’t be anyone left who hasn’t heard of Alan Milburn’s Neets review, let alone read most of it…
items.body: I t’s one of the country’s worst kept secrets. There can’t be anyone left who hasn’t heard of Alan Milburn’s Neets review, let alone read most of it too. It feels as if it’s become part of the fabric of our society for the past six months. There will be a Neets-shaped hole in our lives when it’s over. Not a day has gone by without some part of it being leaked to the media. Seldom has a pitch been so icomprehensively rolled. Milburn has been out and about giving interviews to everyone – regardless of whether they wanted one or not. I rather suspect the reason Royal Mail lied about calling to collect my parcel return yesterday was because the driver found himself cornered by Milburn for a couple of hours and was unable to complete his round. Either that, or Royal Mail has a fleet of vans crisscrossing the country whose sole purpose is to make sure they never deliver anything. Ghost vans.

items.title: FAA pauses installation of new routers after ground stop
items.summary: Problems with the overwhelmed technology led the agency to issue a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday.
items.body: The Federal Aviation Administration said Tuesday it would pause the installation of new routers after problems with the technology led the agency to issue a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday. Tens of thousands of flights were affected by the ground stop, which halted departing flights for more than four hours. It was the longest halt to U.S. flight departures since 9/11. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday that an overloaded router installed in southern Arkansas as part of an upgrade to a system overseen by L3Harris Technologies appeared to overwhelm systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control. The FAA and Department of Transportation have said L3Harris was working to convert the communications network from copper wires to fiber optic.

items.title: US bank services returning to normal after major outage
items.summary: Chase Bank, the largest US bank, said a software bug might be causing the issue, but that it was not "systemic'" or "cyber-related".
items.body: Thousands of customers at major US banks, including JP Morgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Bank of America, reported trouble accessing services, though Chase said its issue has now been resolved. Chase Bank - the largest banking institution in the US - said a "software bug" in its hardware systems was behind the glitch and it was not a cyber security incident. A spokesperson said "this was not a systemic issue" but noted the impact may have affected other banks "only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us". The issue comes after a string of unrelated technical problems, including a massive Microsoft outage and a network failure that grounded all US flights . The problems with the banks started on Monday afternoon. There were almost 5,000 reports of problems with Chase Bank's services, according to the Downdetector website.

items.title: The Guardian view on climate debt: a vicious cycle the world must break at Cop31 | Editorial
items.summary: Poor countries are paying creditors instead of preparing for climate disasters. The international financial system must stop deepening their vulnerability The catastrophe that struck Nepal’s Himalayas in August began with a collapsing glacier. An avalanche of ice and rock…
items.body: T he catastrophe that struck Nepal’s Himalayas in August began with a collapsing glacier. An avalanche of ice and rock unleashed deadly floods, sweeping away villages, bridges and roads, and leaving thousands dead or missing. It illustrated the dangers posed by global heating to the Himalayas’ increasingly unstable glaciers. Nepal lost a tenth of its electricity generation. Reconstruction will cost about $5bn. Yet the Loss and Damage Fund, hailed as a historic breakthrough at the 2022 UN climate summit, has earmarked just $20m for Nepal – less than 5% of the $482m that Kathmandu must pay its external public creditors this year. “The scale of resources needs to increase,” Nepal’s delegation to this year’s UN climate conference drily observed. They are not the only ones agitating for change at Cop31.

items.title: Ukraine damages Putin’s prized Crimea bridge as Zelenskyy lauds ‘unprecedented operation’
items.summary: Ukraine attacked the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea for a second consecutive day, delivering a symbolic blow to President Vladimir Putin.
items.body: Ukraine has damaged the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, delivering a symbolic blow to President Vladimir Putin as Kyiv reels from strikes on its own infrastructure. Sergey Aksyonov, the Russia-installed governor of Crimea, confirmed that the strategically important bridge, which had been briefly closed on Monday, was attacked overnight for the second time in two days. Videos and photos circulating on social media appeared to show the partial destruction of the bridge, with one section having collapsed into the water. CNBC was unable to independently verify the footage. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the attack as an "unprecedented operation" several weeks in the making, with Ukraine's defense forces, security services and weapons manufacturers involved.

items.summary: Stock market debut of Claude AI chatbot maker is expected to be one of the biggest flotations in history The technology company Anthropic is heading for a blockbuster stock market listing this week in what is slated to be one of the largest debuts in history. The company is a…
items.body: The technology company Anthropic is heading for a blockbuster stock market listing this week in what is slated to be one of the largest debuts in history. The company is a leader in artificial intelligence, and is best known for its chatbot Claude. The float, which is expected to value the business at $1.4tn (£1tn), comes at a volatile time for tech stocks, yet it has been reported that the shares could be six times oversubscribed . When a company floats it issues a prospectus for would-be investors that details its activities and lays out the share offering, including an estimated price. Anthropic’s prospectus explains that the shares on sale will be 825m of class A common stock, and that the initial public offering (IPO) price will between $70 and $78 a share. However, the final price will be set on Wednesday.

items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit exposes succession and governance risks for companies and boards
items.summary: The resignation of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO spotlights the missteps of its board and why companies built around one powerful leader creates outsized risk.
items.body: The fallout from Jensen Huang 's affair with an alleged Chinese spy as well as an Nvidia executive that led to his resignation as CEO of Nivida , the company he founded and grew into a $4 trillion chip giant, will likely go on for some time. But the missteps of Nvidia's board of directors offer immediate lessons, say talent and leadership experts. It shows what happens when there's no clear succession plan, the dangers of an overly decentralized leadership structure, and how companies built around one powerful, controlling leader create the kind of risk boards are responsible for preventing.

items.title: Who are the Neets? UK youth job crisis in five charts
items.summary: Bringing the number not in education, employment or training down from a decade high will be tough. Here’s why Alan Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on ‘new deal’ for young people Almost a million young people – one in eight – in the UK are not in education, employment or…
items.body: Almost a million young people – one in eight – in the UK are not in education, employment or training (Neet). Having reached the highest level in a decade, the government is seeking to bring that number down after the recommendations made in Alan Milburn’s landmark report. However, the Neet population is not uniform – making Britain’s youth jobs crisis tougher to respond to. Here we outline the diverse backgrounds of the group struggling to make the transition from school to the world of work on a sustainable basis. An estimated 981,000 of 16- to 24-year-olds in the UK are Neet, accounting for 13% of that age group, according to official figures – close to the highest level since 2014.

"We'll figure it out sometime next year," he told Fox News host Laura Ingraham in an interview that aired Monday evening. "I'm not an expert in this but my understanding with a presidential campaign is there's a lot of infrastructure that you have to set up, fundraising, all that stuff and so you can't declare a month before the Iowa caucus that you're going to run for president," he said. "So, you know, I haven't made a decision." Vance has yet to openly declare any ambition to succeed President Donald Trump when his current term ends, but speculation that the vice president has his sights set on the White House has been mounting for some time. items.title: Neet ideas: what’s in Alan Milburn’s report on young people not in education, employment or training?
items.summary: Former minister’s 278-page report calls for changes to employment regulations, education, healthcare and benefits Who are the Neets? UK youth job crisis in five charts Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on young people Five months on from a first report detailing the…
items.body: Five months on from a first report detailing the growing crisis of young people who are not in education, employment or training (Neet), Alan Milburn has produced his recommendations on how to tackle it. Set out over 278 pages, they amount to, as he readily accepts, a major rethink of everything from employment regulations to education, healthcare and benefits. While this was in part covered by the first report, Milburn is at pains to begin the new volume with his belief that the issue of Neets is not a failure of the younger generation but a case of them being let down by a series of structural factors. “The young people I have met over the last year are not asking for an easier life. They are asking for a fair chance to build one,” he writes. The answer must be radical, he says. “This cannot be fixed by tweaking the edges of the existing system.

items.title: Trump’s accounts traded up to $97.5 million in Nvidia as Huang gained White House access
items.summary: Trump’s accounts sold up to $1 million in Nvidia stock five days after he was briefed on Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
items.body: The chipmaker helped propel the stock market that Trump is fond of touting. Its billionaire co-founder, Jensen Huang , became one of the president's favorite businessmen. And by the end of last year, Nvidia had become one of Trump's three largest individual stock holdings, worth between $12.5 million and $58 million, up from between $615,000 and $1.3 million a year earlier. Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 103 times — transactions worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million, according to a new CNBC analysis of his annual and periodic financial disclosures, which were most recently updated through August. By midday Monday, Trump's Nvidia stake, based on the value he reported holding in August, would be worth $4.5 million to $57.7 million with stock priced around $157.

items.title: The corporate boom in vegan food is dead. Long live real plant-based cooking | Isobel Lewis
items.summary: The fad for plant-based junk food has run its course, but restaurants reflecting the centuries-long history of this cuisine still thrive Have you ever gone to make a restaurant reservation and been met with a Google Maps listing bearing that harbinger of doom: “Permanently…
items.body: H ave you ever gone to make a restaurant reservation and been met with a Google Maps listing bearing that harbinger of doom: “Permanently closed”? It’s a pretty deflating feeling – and one the UK’s vegan population knows well. Over the past few years, many once-beloved, plant-based establishments have shut up shop or moved away from brick-and-mortar businesses, from The Allotment in Manchester to The Vurger Co, which had restaurants in London and Brighton. Each shuttering galvanises the vegan community into supporting their local spots. But they’re gutting too, and deeply felt by a group who see themselves more as an ethically motivated community than simply clientele. The so-called sorry state of the vegan restaurant scene has been widely reported on (not least by me ).

items.title: CNBC's The China Connection newsletter: As Nike and Lululemon struggle in China, Xiaohongshu is helping local brands take off
items.summary: There's one formula for success behind the rise of trendy new Chinese fashion brands, according to Euromonitor International.
items.body: Hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing. Welcome to the latest edition of The China Connection — a snapshot of what I'm seeing and hearing from local businesses. While the world watched the Nvidia saga around Jensen Huang unfold, Chinese retailers quietly wrapped up the local version of Black Friday, known as Singles Day. What can foreign brands learn? As Lululemon , On Running and other Western consumer brands have sought to expand in China, so have a crop of local brands with English names. Monday Sleeping Club, Crying Center, AW Project, an action a day, Liegee. The list of trendy new Chinese brands has grown rapidly, despite flatlining retail sales nationwide . "Their success rests on one shared formula," said Cynthia Zhang, analyst, Euromonitor International.

items.body: Imperial Brands, the owner of Davidoff cigarettes and Blu vapes, is cutting up to 4,600 jobs in a huge cost-saving drive as it uses more AI and other technologies. The Bristol-based company said this year 2,100 roles would go globally, and it plans a further reduction of between 2,100 and 2,500 jobs by the end of 2030. Imperial Brands, which has a global workforce of about 25,000 people, will close its Langenhagen factory in Germany next year and has sold a plant in Taiwan, leading to 700 job losses. It intends to outsource 400 jobs to Capgemini from its finance and procurement teams in Krakow, Poland and global supply chain centre in Warsaw. The company is holding consultations on the planned reductions in several countries. The current cuts affect a small number of jobs in the UK.

items.title: Deutsche Bank shares sink as whistleblowers reveal Epstein payments, Trump tax leak, Russia bets
items.summary: A 15-million-file leak details alleged control failures at Deutsche Bank, including Epstein-linked payments and a Trump tax blunder.
items.body: Deutsche Bank shares fell sharply in early trading on Tuesday after whistleblowers leaked about 15 million files from the German lender, with media reports revealing alleged historic failures across its risk management and financial crime controls. These include suspicious payments linked to late financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and accidental leaks of President Donald Trump 's tax statements. The leaks contain board minutes, emails, internal investigations and other material that point to systemic failures across the Frankfurt-listed lender's business functions stretching back two decades. Shares in Deutsche Bank were 4.7% lower by 9:20 a.m. E.T., having fallen more than 6% in early trade in Frankfurt. Deutsche Bank processed $582 million in suspicious payments linked to Jeffrey Epstein, far more than previously known, the FT reported .

items.body: David Beckham’s company reacted with “shock and dismay” after discovering his branded fragrance range was on sale in petrol stations and in the British discount store Poundland, court documents have revealed. The former England football captain’s brand, DB Ventures, has launched a lawsuit against the distributor of the products, arguing it allowed them to be sold in stores that had not been agreed upon. DB Ventures claimed to have discovered the perfumes for sale in the troubled UK budget retailer and in a “bargain bin inside a gas station” at an unspecified location, according to court papers filed in New York. items.title: Investor Steve Eisman says the AI neocloud stocks are in 'big trouble' from Nvidia fallout
items.summary: Steve Eisman is appearing on "Squawk Box" on Tuesday.
items.body: Investor Steve Eisman said the so-called AI neocloud stocks will be the biggest losers from the unfolding Nvidia scandal. Nvidia was essentially a "virtual vertical holding company and it's unwinding," said Eisman of "Big Short" fame on CNBC's "Squawk Box ." "I think neoclouds are all in big trouble though because they are part of that vertical holding company and I think they're about to get ejected." Neoclouds, which used borrowed funds to build data centers, have been among the hardest-hit stocks during the recent pullback in the artificial intelligence trade. CoreWeave and Nebius are each down more than 50% the last three months. All eyes on Wall Street are on chipmaker Nvidia as it reports earnings on Tuesday after the bell while grappling with a potential Chinese espionage scandal.

Rob Bonta, California’s attorney general, said the “infamous” attack was just one of 80 known incidents involving “loss of control” and shows that OpenAI doesn’t have adequate safeguards in place to protect society.

items.title: U.S. agencies say they initiated investigation into Nvidia partner Megaspeed in 2024
items.summary: The Commerce and Justice departments said in a joint statement that U.S. investigations into Megaspeed began in 2024.
items.body: The U.S. Commerce and Justice Department on Monday stateside said they had initiated an investigation into Singapore-based company Megaspeed in 2024 to "address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting." Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia, has been drawn into the fallout surrounding the leadership shake-up at chip giant Nvidia . In a joint release, the departments outlined a timeline of their investigations into Megaspeed, saying the probes began in 2024 over potential export-control violations. In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list, after Commerce Department investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to the company. items.title: Singapore, Malaysia grapple with US chip curbs targeting Southeast Asia
items.body: SINGAPORE/KUALA LUMPUR/BANGKOK -- Southeast Asian nations that have been boosted by investment related to the AI boom are reeling as the U.S. tightens controls on chip exports to their economies over fears the region could be a waypoint for illicitly shipping semiconductors to China.
